title: Why Prices Are Never Supposed to Go Back Down

beats.text: Central banks want your lemonade to cost more every year. On purpose.
Penny's lemonade costs a dollar. Next year, a dollar and two cents. The year after, a dollar and four.
That's two percent inflation. And America's central bank has officially aimed for exactly that since twenty twelve.
Why not zero? Why not let prices fall?
Because if you knew lemonade would be cheaper next week, you'd wait.
So would everyone. Penny sells less. She cuts hours. People earn less, so they spend less, so prices fall again.
In the Great Depression, American prices fell by about a quarter in four years. It was a disaster.
So central banks aim a little above zero. Prices creep up slowly, so nobody waits.
The goal isn't cheaper lemonade. It's wages that rise faster than lemonade does.
So next time prices tick up two percent, that's not the system failing. It's the system working. Because
